title: Vowel letters
topic: א ה ו י as vowels; full spelling (ktiv male)
why: A first step toward reading "the Israeli way": full spelling replaces some of the dots with the letters ו, י, ה and א. Each word is shown with and then without vowels, to prepare for reading without niqqud in the next lesson.

Reading without the dots

Open an Israeli newspaper, look at a street sign or a message on a phone: no niqqud. Israelis read without vowels, a bit like you do when you recognize \"thx\" or \"pls\" in a text message: you know the word, you don't need to see all of it.

To help the reader, spelling without vowels, full spelling (כְּתִיב מָלֵא, ktiv male), keeps or adds four letters that act as vowels: ו, י, ה and א.

With vowelsWithout vowelsSound
שָׁלוֹםשלוםshalom
תּוֹדָהתודהtoda
טוֹבטובtov
מִימיmi
הוּאהואhu

Good news: in these words, the ו for o and u, and the י for i, are already letters. When the dots go away, they stay.

Without the dots, the dagesh disappears too: ב can be read b or v, כ k or kh, פ p or f. It's the word you know that tells you: אבא is read aba, כלב is read kelev.

", "

ו and י: o, u, i

Without niqqud, the language adds a letter where there was only a dot. The o is written ו, the u is written ו, the i is often written י:

SoundWith vowelsWithout vowelsMeaning
oבֹּקֶרבוקרmorning [boker]
oנֹעָהנועהNoa [No'a]
uשֻׁלְחָןשולחןtable [shulkhan]
iסִפּוּרסיפורstory [sipur]
iעִתּוֹןעיתוןnewspaper [iton]
e (sometimes)בֵּיצָהביצהegg [beitsa]

A few exceptions: some very common little words keep their short form, לא, זאת, פה (lo, zot, po), and sometimes the i stays invisible: ישראל (Israel), עברית (ivrit, Hebrew).

The trap: a ו can be read o, u… or v! דוד is read dod (uncle) or David. And two וו in the middle of a word make a v: טלוויזיה (televizya).

", "

ה and א: a and e at the end of a word

The a and the e usually leave no trace in the middle of a word: שַׁבָּת becomes שבת, כֶּלֶב becomes כלב, יֶלֶד becomes ילד. That's where an English speaker gets stuck: all you see is three consonants. An Israeli reader adds the vowels of the word they know in their head.

At the end of a word, a silent ה or א often signals a or e:

End of wordWith vowelsWithout vowelsSound
ה = aתּוֹדָהתודהtoda
ה = aיַלְדָּהילדהyalda
ה = eקָפֶהקפהkafe
ה = eמוֹרֶהמורהmore
א = aסָבָאסבאsaba

As a result: מורה is read more (a male teacher) or mora (a female teacher). Context decides: that will be the topic of the next lesson.

The א also stays in the middle of words, always silent: מְאוֹד is written מאוד (me'od).
